target_customer: Urban Indian households in Bengaluru, Mumbai and other cities that want milk and groceries delivered before 7 am by subscription
problem: Last-mile grocery delivery in India is costly per order; daily milk subscriptions give a recurring route that can carry other groceries cheaply.
business_model: Subscription daily delivery of milk and groceries with a delivery margin

founders.name: Puneet Kumar
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a two-time founder; later roles (Nexus venture partner, YC visiting partner) came after Supr Daily. IIT Bombay is reported in search results but not on a page I opened, so education is null.

technical_complexity.rationale: Consumer app plus route and inventory logistics for daily early-morning delivery; hard part was operations, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Daily subscriptions and route density gave some habit lock-in, but milk delivery is low margin and rivals such as BigBasket and Milkbasket could replicate it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Swiggy acquired it in 2018 (sources disagree on the year), and BigBasket's daily service and later DailyNinja purchase (March 2020) show incumbents moved into the segment.

market_need_then: Indian households rely on daily milk and essentials delivery; the company's own pitch is that the milk route cuts last-mile cost. No dated survey or spend figure was opened.

branding.name_origin: Not explained. The YC page uses the phrase Trojan Cow for milk as the wedge that carries all groceries.

identity.voice_and_tone: Habit and family stories; first brand campaign #BeSuprDaily in February 2020 built on customer stories.

branding.brand_signature: Trojan Cow framing for the milk-first strategy

brand_strength.rationale: A first brand campaign only arrived in 2020; no mascot, press on the brand or community was found. It was folded into Swiggy's operations.

outcome_analysis: Supr Daily used milk subscriptions to deliver groceries and, per its YC page, reached a 100 million dollar revenue run rate across six cities with over 200 thousand daily orders after Swiggy acquired it. Swiggy later restructured it: founders left in 2021 and in May 2022 service was suspended in five of six cities. The scale was real but the model depended on Swiggy's subsidy of a low margin business, and the early exit price was not disclosed.
notes: Seed amounts: Rs 10 crore (about 1.5M USD) in May 2017 appears in Entrackr and TechCrunch listings. Acquisition year conflicts (CB Insights Sept 2018, other pages 2019 or 2021); 2018 used. No website listed in the directory, so there is no site fetch. Competitor search returned only 2018 to 2020 sources (Milkbasket, DailyNinja, BB Daily), so the list is empty. The failure factors reflect Swiggy's 2022 cutback as reported; the stated reason was restructuring for business fit, and the unit economics link is an inference.
